title: Ami of Vardina
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Beitzah 27b: Ami of Vardina used to examine the firstborn animals of the Patriarch’s house; on a festival he would not examine. They came and told Rabbi Ami, who said: “He does well” (Rashi explains: he was handsome and was named after roses; but Hyman suggests [he was named] after the place called Vardina, as in Eruvin 49a). In Niddah 19b: “Ami of Vardina said that Rabbi Abbahu said,” and there too Rashi explains as in Beitzah 27b, writing there that in Gittin 41a he is called Ami Shapir Na’eh. There he spoke in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said of him: “Because Ami is handsome, does he say teachings that are not handsome?”

notes.text: Rashi’s rose/beauty interpretation and Hyman’s proposed geographical Vardina explanation remain competing attributed interpretations. No place-derived identity is silently established.

The firstborn-examiner episode is directly present in the consulted Beitzah 27a:15; Hyman’s supplied 27b reference is preserved. The roses/beauty explanation is reported from Rashi, while origin in a place called Vardina is Hyman’s suggestion. Neither explanation establishes a geographical identity here.
